Table 8-5 shows the estimated capital cost of Bad Creek and the alternative projects. In order to facilitate comparison and provide the amount of power needed to meet the estimated system demand and reserve requirements, the alternative potential sites were sized to duplicate Bad Creek power operation. Further, more detailed studies of the alternative sites might show that additional capacity could be added which might result in economies of scale. A larger installation, with subsequent lower unit costs, could result in lower total system costs in future years as the system demand increases to the extent that additional pumped storage capacity is needed. However, fixed charges would have to be carried on the unused plant. The alternatives have the advantage over other sites studied outside the Jocassee area in that they would all use the existing Jocassee Lake as a lower reservoir, thus eliminating the cost of a lower dam. Also being close to the source of pumping energy from the Oconee nuclear plant, they would have lower transmission line costs.
The Long Spur Ridge Project is suitable and economically attractive for higher capacity development. If this project is sized to the capacity needs of the 1985 load level with provisions for the ultimate capacity installation, it would result in higher capital investment. For these reasons the Applicant proposes the Bad Creek site over Long Spur Ridge, so as to maintain its option to develop the latter site at some future date at a higher capacity, when such a capability could be developed in a reasonable time-frame. If, on the other hand, the site is developed to meet 1985 load demand only, as Staff has done, the project would lose the economic attractiveness of the higher capacity for meeting the greater load demand at the future date.
Geologically the alternative sites to the proposed Bad Creek site are very similar, having the same basic rock types, soils, slopes, and watershed conditions. Lacking detailed geologic and foundation data for the alternative locations, however, it is not known whether the same geologic constraints would apply.
If the proposed Bad Creek Project is constructed and found to be economical and successful in the system, these additional alternative projects could be considered in any later program of expansion.
